title: The Immortal Game
summary: London, 1851: Adolf Anderssen gives up his queen, both rooks and a bishop, and checkmates anyway.

steps.title: London, 1851
steps.text: The year is 1851 and the world's best players have gathered in London for the first international chess tournament. During a break, the German master Adolf Anderssen sits down for a friendly game against Lionel Kieseritzky. What follows becomes the most famous game ever played: the Immortal Game. Press play and watch it happen.
steps.narration: London, 1851. The first international chess tournament in history. In a side room, Adolf Anderssen plays a friendly game that will become the most famous of all time. Press play and watch.

steps.title: Anderssen – Kieseritzky, London 1851
steps.text: Anderssen plays the King's Gambit, the favorite weapon of chess's romantic era, when attack was everything and material was just a price to pay. The captions tell the story as the game rolls.
steps.narration: Anderssen opens with the King's Gambit, the swaggering weapon of the romantic era. Watch what he does with it.

notes.text: The King's Gambit: White offers a pawn for a head start in development. Black accepts.
5.Bxb5: Kieseritzky tried to chase the bishop away with ...b5. Anderssen simply takes the pawn.
11.Rg1! The rook joins the attack. In this era, material meant nothing: only the enemy king mattered.
17.Nd5! Anderssen is behind in material, yet every one of his pieces is hunting the black king.
18.Bd6!! The famous move. Anderssen offers BOTH of his rooks.
19...Qxa1+: …and then the second one. But the black queen is now far away from her own king.
21.Nxg7+ Kd8: the black king is trapped in the middle of the board.
22.Qf6+!! A queen sacrifice, forcing mate. If the knight takes, the bishop lands on e7.
23.Be7# Checkmate! Down a queen, two rooks and a bishop, Anderssen mates with his three little pieces. The Immortal Game.

steps.title: You be Anderssen
steps.prompt: Black's king is cornered and his queen is off in the corner of the board. Find Anderssen's immortal finish.
steps.hint: The queen can give herself up: if it clears the road to e7 for the bishop on d6.
steps.success: Qf6+!! Nxf6 Be7#: the most famous checkmate of the nineteenth century. You found the immortal finish.

steps.title: The romantic era
steps.question: The Immortal Game is the symbol of chess's romantic era. What did that style value above everything else?

options.text: Daring sacrifices and direct attacks on the king
options.why: Exactly. Players like Anderssen happily gave up whole rooks and queens if it led to the enemy king.

options.text: Slow pawn maneuvering and careful defense
options.why: That style came later, with Steinitz. The romantics wanted fireworks, not safety.
Endgame science was barely born in 1851: these games were decided by attacks long before an endgame.

steps.narration: One last question about the era this game created.
